memories.content: Link expected participant burden in each user study task to its corresponding mitigation strategy.
Specify the accommodations necessary for participants to access the prototype and research tasks.
Specify how accessibility accommodations will be provided during user study sessions.
Describe how personal identifiers will be separated from research data immediately after collection.
Specify the equipment to be loaned to participants who lack necessary devices.
Describe the procedure for returning equipment loaned to participants.
HCI ethics reviewers verify that expected burdens and mitigation strategies correspond to each user study task.
Inform participants that the formative evaluation prototype is not a finished service.
Set an upper limit on cumulative task burden when requesting repeated evaluations from the same participant.
The author of this proposal tends to emphasize expected benefits of the prototype over participant burden.
In organizations where leaders or institutional staff handle recruitment, recruitment authority and academic or professional evaluation authority may be combined in the same role.
Use an em dash only for a deliberate interruption or sharp contrast; otherwise split the sentence or choose ordinary punctuation.
In procedural passages, begin each sentence with the action, condition, or output instead of repeating “we” so the steps remain easy to follow and reuse.
Write system behaviors confirmed in the actual usage environment as observed states.
Write system behaviors not yet confirmed in the field as conditional plans.
Readers can reconstruct a sequence more accurately when each sentence begins with the action or condition rather than the author.
Do not mechanically split connected thoughts into separate short sentences when doing so destroys the intended reading rhythm.
Preserve a longer sentence when its clauses form one continuous movement that is easier to follow together than apart.
The user understands that short sentences are easier to scan but feels that uniformly segmented prose loses its reading rhythm.
Write procedural sentences so their opening phrase can be reused as a checklist item without changing the step's meaning.
The user should choose “I” as an individual author or “we” for a named team and should not mix them when describing the same responsible party.
Action-first procedural sentences can be reordered or copied into a checklist more easily because their subject is the step rather than the proposal author.
The user can explain whether an em dash marks an intentional interruption or contrast rather than using it decoratively.
An em dash creates a stronger interruption than a comma and can make a deliberate contrast easier to hear in the sentence.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate domains rather than shared or competing policies. The reference frame defines participant-protection and study-access requirements, while the compared frame defines prose style, procedural clarity, evidentiary phrasing, sentence rhythm, and authorial voice conventions.

relations.reason: These memories express directive and review aspects of one reference-only task-level burden-control requirement; the compared frame contains no corresponding writing-policy claim.
relations.summary: Expected burdens and their mitigations are mapped to individual user-study tasks and checked by ethics reviewers.

relations.reason: These memories split the identification and provision stages of one reference-only accommodation plan; the compared frame provides no corresponding accessibility requirement.
relations.summary: Accessibility planning identifies necessary accommodations and specifies how they will be delivered during study sessions.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful reference-only data-protection procedure with no corresponding claim in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Personal identifiers are separated from research data immediately after collection.

relations.reason: These memories describe complementary stages of one reference-only equipment-loan lifecycle; the compared frame contains no corresponding operational requirement.
relations.summary: Participant equipment loans specify both the devices provided and the return procedure.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful reference-only participant disclosure with no corresponding claim in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Participants are told that the formative-evaluation prototype is not a finished service.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful reference-only safeguard for repeated participation with no corresponding claim in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Repeated evaluations involving the same participant are subject to an upper limit on cumulative task burden.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful reference-only observation about authorial bias, distinct from the compared frame’s general prose conventions.
relations.summary: The proposal author tends to emphasize prototype benefits over participant burden.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful reference-only observation about institutional role concentration with no corresponding claim in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Recruitment authority and academic or professional evaluation authority may be combined when organizational leaders or staff recruit participants.

relations.reason: These memories provide the rule, rationale, and user-understanding aspect of one compared-only punctuation policy; the reference frame contains no corresponding style claim.
relations.summary: Em dashes are reserved for intentional interruption or sharp contrast, whose stronger audible break should be explainable rather than decorative.

relations.reason: These memories restate the rule and practical benefits of one compared-only action-first procedure style; the reference frame contains no corresponding writing convention.
relations.summary: Procedural sentences begin with the action, condition, or output so sequences remain clear and steps can be reordered or reused as checklist items.

relations.reason: These memories split one compared-only phrasing policy according to explicit confirmation status; the reference frame contains no corresponding evidentiary-language rule.
relations.summary: System behavior is written as an observed state when confirmed in actual use and as a conditional plan when field confirmation is absent.

relations.reason: These memories state the preference, rule, and preservation condition for one compared-only sentence-rhythm policy; the reference frame contains no corresponding prose claim.
relations.summary: Connected thoughts remain in a longer sentence when splitting them would impair continuity or the intended reading rhythm.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful compared-only authorial-voice convention with no corresponding claim in the reference frame.
relations.summary: An author chooses “I” for an individual or “we” for a named team and uses that voice consistently for the same responsible party.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame covers deliberate em-dash use, action-first reusable procedures, field-confirmed versus conditional claims, sentence rhythm, and consistent authorial voice.
reports.reference_only: The reference frame covers burden mitigation and limits, accommodations, data de-identification, equipment loans, prototype disclosure, author bias, and recruitment power risks.
